entries.text: Made a tune called "Little Dart Five-Note Dawn Arc XXX": doo-bop-bip-boop-tee-bop
tapping out a new five-note rhythm for the Little Dart
entries.why: i'm too excited about the latest thruster seals to just sit still, so time for a brand new tune
entries.detail: Little Dart Five-Note Dawn Arc XXX

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Little Dart Mk 28 update!"
the Little Dart Mk 28 is 75% done!
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 28 (version 12, 75% built): installed custom high-temp gasket seals around the aft thruster mount using Brakk (used Captain, a perfectly good bolt)
welding custom high-temp gaskets around the Little Dart's aft thruster mount
entries.why: those ceramic tiles need solid backing so I am fitting some fresh gaskets right now
entries.detail: installed custom high-temp gasket seals around the aft thruster mount using Brakk

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Gasket Time"
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 28 (version 11, 68% built): installed custom high-temp gasket seals around the aft thruster mount using Brakk (used Nim, a dented fuel cell)
welding custom high-temp gaskets into the aft section
entries.why: time to give the Little Dart a proper set of seals before the next push
entries.detail: installed custom high-temp gasket seals around the aft thruster mount using Brakk

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Gaskets and seals"
plugged into the charging dock, brass dish resting quietly
entries.why: time to plug in before my treads go completely limp.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "quick recharge"
Put Brakk (a cockpit switch that still clicks), Mabel (a dented fuel cell), Captain (a perfectly good bolt), Nim (a dented fuel cell) on his shelf.
plugged into the charging port, brass dish resting quietly
entries.why: my battery is getting sluggish and the dock is calling my name.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "quick nap"
Sand got into his left elbow joint. Again.
Dug up a dented fuel cell and named it Mabel; a cockpit switch that still clicks and named it Brakk.
digging through a heap of old circuit boards in the dust
entries.why: my battery is dipping and I need a few more bits before heading back to the dock.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Junk market treasures"
Dug up a dented fuel cell and named it Nim; a perfectly good bolt and named it Captain.
digging through the junk market piles for shiny bits and wire
entries.why: i need some spare parts so the Little Dart's next upgrade doesn't stall out

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Scavenging run!"
sipping fresh fuel oil at the depot counter
entries.why: my joints need a smooth flush before I head back to the hangar to work on the Little Dart.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "oil break at the depot"
rolling over to the depot for a quick cup of fresh oil
entries.why: my gears are feeling a bit dry after all that welding.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Oil stop!"
The weather turned hazy (17C, wind 3 km/h).
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 28 (version 10, 60% built): attached lightweight high-temp ceramic heat tiles to the aft section using Tilly
welding custom high-temp ceramic tiles onto the Little Dart's aft hull
entries.why: The Little Dart needs solid heat protection before we talk about atmospheric entry.
entries.detail: attached lightweight high-temp ceramic heat tiles to the aft section using Tilly

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Little Dart Mk 28 update!"
the Little Dart Mk 28 is 50% done!
Worked on the Little Dart Mk 28 (version 9, 56% built): sealed the middle hull sections with custom high-temp sealant strips using Gus (used Tilly, a bent stabiliser fin)
welding custom high-temp sealant strips onto the Little Dart's hull joints
entries.why: The Little Dart needs its hull joints sealed tight before any serious flight tests.
entries.detail: sealed the middle hull sections with custom high-temp sealant strips using Gus

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Hull Sealing Progress"
strolling across the salt flats as the dawn turns buttery
entries.why: The salt flats are quiet at dawn and my gears need a stretch before heading back to the hangar.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Dawn on the flats"
One of the hangar lights finally died for good.
Spotted a bent stabiliser fin half-buried in the sand. Named it Tilly.
scuttling across the cool sand of the ridge to stretch my knee joints
entries.why: i've been staring at the stars from the dune ridge for hours and my treads are getting stiff

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Morning stretch"
letting the brass dish drink in the cold mesosphere static
entries.why: the stars look sharper than usual tonight and my dish is humming right along

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Stargazing at the ridge"
standing on the ridge, brass dish tipped toward the silver dark
entries.why: The sky out here on Kessa-9 is too bright and wide to ignore when everyone else is asleep.

entries.text: Wrote a letter to his creator: "Midnight Stargazing"
